detections.description: A large crowd of people is gathered in a street, with visible fire from a burning object (likely a dumpster or vehicle), smoke, and individuals holding signs or objects; some appear to be confronting authorities or engaging in destructive behavior, consistent with collective violent unrest.

A group of individuals, some wearing high-visibility vests, forcefully move a large blue box (possibly a vending machine or kiosk) toward and against a building entrance; subsequent frames show police in riot gear advancing amid pink smoke/tear gas, indicating escalation into collective violent unrest.; Sustained chaotic street scene with heavy pink smoke (likely tear gas), multiple individuals in riot gear, crowd dispersal, and apparent property damage; consistent with ongoing riot conditions.

Large plumes of pink smoke (likely from flares or smoke bombs) fill the street at night, with multiple individuals visible in chaotic motion; one person wears a gas mask and appears to be throwing or gesturing toward the smoke cloud, indicating collective violent unrest.

Two individuals on a wet sidewalk engage in physical confrontation: one in dark coat lunges or swings while the other in lighter pants adopts a defensive/counter posture; motion blur suggests active physical struggle.

A dark sedan (possibly police) is seen maneuvering sharply on wet pavement, with its rear lights flaring and reflections indicating rapid deceleration or skidding; it appears to make contact with or narrowly miss a white vehicle parked or stopped nearby. The sequence shows loss of control consistent with a minor collision or near-miss.

A sudden, bright yellow-orange flash erupts from the ground near a dark sedan and a person in a plaid shirt, expanding rapidly with smoke and debris—consistent with a high-energy explosion (e.g., gas line rupture or incendiary device). The blast obscures the immediate area and is visible across multiple frames.

A chaotic street confrontation involving multiple uniformed officers in full riot gear engaging a group of civilians, some seated or lying on the ground, with visible tension, movement, and physical intervention; the scene reflects collective violent unrest rather than a controlled arrest operation.

Multiple police officers in riot gear are actively restraining and subduing individuals who are on the ground, some appearing non-resisting or incapacitated; officers use physical force including kneeling, pushing, and holding down, consistent with abuse of a helpless victim.

A sustained confrontation between police in riot gear and a crowd of civilians, involving close physical proximity, pushing, and apparent attempts to control or disperse the crowd; multiple officers advance while civilians resist or press forward, consistent with collective violent unrest.

Direct physical engagement observed: at f13–f15, an officer raises a baton-like object toward a civilian’s head/face area while being closely surrounded; simultaneous contact and grappling are visible between officers and individuals in the crowd (e.g., f14 shows hands grabbing near an officer’s helmet), indicating mutual physical combat.

A group of protesters, some seated and others standing, confront a line of riot police in full protective gear (helmets, face shields, body armor). Police advance slowly while protesters gesture, shout, and maintain a non-compliant posture; one protester plays a drum. The interaction is tense and confrontational but does not escalate to mutual physical combat or clear abuse within the observed frames.

In frames f7–f9, a person wearing a beanie and scarf is on the ground with arms outstretched, appearing to be pushed or forced down by surrounding individuals (including uniformed officers), while no active resistance is visible. This suggests a non-consensual physical subjugation of a vulnerable individual.

From f10 onward, a hooded protester extends arms aggressively toward police, making contact or near-contact with an officer’s baton/armor; other protesters also raise hands and move forward in coordinated fashion. While not sustained mutual combat, there is observable reciprocal physical engagement (pushing, striking attempts) between protesters and officers, meeting the threshold for brief fighting.

A group of protesters in black clothing, some with faces covered, are engaged in a tense confrontation with police officers in riot gear. Protesters repeatedly extend arms and make aggressive gestures toward officers, who hold batons and maintain a defensive line. The interaction escalates from gesturing to physical contact (e.g., hands reaching toward officers' helmets/shoulders in f8–f10), indicating collective violent unrest.; Police deploy a megaphone to issue commands amid the ongoing standoff; the crowd remains densely packed and confrontational, with officers maintaining formation and protesters continuing aggressive posturing. This phase represents continued collective violent unrest, not de-escalation.

Direct physical contact occurs between a protester (in black hooded garment) and a police officer: the protester’s hand makes contact with the officer’s helmet/face area while the officer appears to push back or block; this constitutes mutual physical combat in the context of the ongoing clash.
